reason: The Go module github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk v0.20.0 gives ACP framing and message types in both roles the harness needs (agent side for the ACP front end, client side for the ACP subagent provider and tests); it is pre-1.0, so only one harness package may import it.

Upstream uses the SDK to find, start and parse a bundled Claude Code executable and to refuse interactive requests; the Go provider starts the user's installed claude executable in print mode with streaming JSON output and command-line flags that do the same, with no SDK and no vendor binary in the release.

The owner keeps the OAR runtime bridge. Upstream embeds a patched copy of the JavaScript library in its provider; the Go provider instead runs the OAR the operator installed as a host-owned child process and talks to it over a line-delimited JSON protocol, so all seven runtime ids keep a path, nothing of OAR is linked or patched, and the operator must install Node 24 or later, the OAR package and each native agent. No Go module for OAR could be verified.

Upstream imports no code from this package; it only runs the bundled executable as 'app-server --stdio' and speaks JSON-RPC to it. The Go provider does the same with the Codex executable the user installed, over the harness's own NDJSON JSON-RPC codec.

The harness neither ships nor edits OAR, so there is no distributed file to patch. The three fixes (an explicit permission mode is not overridden by skip-all, a failed start waits for the process to exit, installation probes use the run's environment) are requirements DH-LIB-OAR-R1 to R3. The bridge meets them from outside OAR, by owning the child process tree and its environment and by refusing an instance that states no permission posture; the two product providers meet them in their own code. Each has a test.

The exemption lets pnpm install the per-platform Claude Code executable package @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64 before its release-age window ends. The Go build downloads and ships no Anthropic software; the provider starts the Claude Code the user installed, and the version question becomes a run-time check (DH-LIB-CLAUDEAGENTSDK-R2).

The exemption exists to install one exact patched OAR release through npm when upstream is built. Building the Go harness downloads no OAR package, so no package-age rule applies and nothing is exempted; which OAR release runs is the operator's choice, and the bridge reports the version it found and refuses one outside its supported range.

The single version-union exemption lets pnpm install the Codex package and its six platform executables before their release-age window ends. The Go build downloads and ships no Codex executable; the provider starts the Codex the user installed and checks its version at run time (DH-LIB-CODEX-R2).
